note: Verified public reference registry for the educational synthetic benchmark study. Contains only verified real-world methodological and background sources.

references.title: Multi-omics microsampling for the profiling of lifestyle-associated changes in health
references.supported_scope: Demonstrates molecular profiling of lifestyle-associated physiological changes from 10 uL blood microsamples; both online year (2023) and issue year (2024) are valid bibliographic dates. Does not establish universal clinical disease prediction.

references.authors: Vaswani, Ashish; Shazeer, Noam; Parmar, Niki; Uszkoreit, Jakob; Jones, Llion; Gomez, Aidan N.; Kaiser, Lukasz; Polosukhin, Illia
references.title: Attention Is All You Need
references.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS) 30, 5998-6008
references.supported_scope: Defines the scaled dot-product and multi-head self-attention architecture used for neural sequence and token representation.

references.authors: Pajouheshnia, Romin; Groenwold, Rolf H. H.; Peelen, Linda M.; Moons, Karel G. M.; Reitsma, Joris B.
references.title: How variation in predictor measurement affects the discriminative ability and transportability of a prediction model
references.supported_scope: Analyzes how predictor measurement heterogeneity across settings affects model discrimination and transportability; online publication in 2018 and volume publication in 2019 are both accurate.

references.authors: Zech, John R.; Badgeley, Marcus A.; Liu, Manway; Costa, Anthony B.; Titano, Joseph J.; Oermann, Eric Karl
references.title: Variable generalization performance of a deep learning model to detect pneumonia in chest radiographs: A cross-sectional study
references.supported_scope: Shows that site-specific prevalence differences and institutional confounding can inflate internal split performance while failing to generalize to external hospital cohorts.

references.authors: Smith, Lloyd M.; Kelleher, Neil L.; The Consortium for Top Down Proteomics
references.title: Proteoform: a single term describing protein complexity
references.supported_scope: Establishes the technical term 'proteoform' to designate all molecular forms of a protein product arising from a single gene via genetic variation, alternative splicing, and post-translational modifications.

references.title: Selection bias in gene extraction on the basis of microarray gene-expression data
references.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (PNAS) 99(10), 6562-6566
references.supported_scope: Demonstrates optimistic selection bias when evaluation samples leak into feature extraction or fitting steps outside the training loop.

references.title: scikit-learn User Guide and API Reference: Common pitfalls and recommended practices; sklearn.metrics.roc_auc_score; Tuning the decision threshold for class prediction
references.supported_scope: Documents fitting transformers strictly on training data before transforming test data, computing AUROC from continuous scores, and selecting classification thresholds on validation data separate from final test evaluation.

references.title: The Precision-Recall Plot Is More Informative than the ROC Plot When Evaluating Binary Classifiers on Imbalanced Datasets
references.supported_scope: Explains why precision-recall (AP/AUPRC) depends on positive class prevalence and why class proportions must be reported alongside ROC and PR metrics.

references.title: Hydra v1.3 Documentation: Output/Working directory
references.supported_scope: Describes the .hydra output subdirectory (config.yaml, hydra.yaml, overrides.yaml) generated per run.

references.title: Attention is not Explanation
references.supported_scope: Shows that attention weights often fail to correlate with gradient-based feature importance and that counterfactual attention distributions can yield identical predictions.

references.title: Attention is not not Explanation
references.supported_scope: Provides diagnostic conditions under which attention distributions can offer plausible internal model explanations, without implying biological causality or clinical target validation.
